title: Existing-Home Sales (NAR, October 2026 data) — the unconfounded control edition, 10:00 a.m. ET on a session no GDPNow vintage touches
source: IR: the publisher's own forward calendar — nar.realtor/newsroom/nar-statistical-news-release-schedule, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 483,177 bytes), whose 2026 table reads verbatim "NOVEMBER | Thu., Nov. 12 | October Existing-Home Sales" under the page's standing note "All releases are distributed at 10 a.m. Eastern Time", and its downloadable twin /sites/default/files/2025-11/2026-nar-statistical-news-release-schedule.docx (HTTP 200, 55,384 bytes, published 2025-11), whose November block carries the same row. Promoted from the `EST:` proposal filed 2026-09-06 by the existing-home-sales-2026-12-09 adjacency sweep, on the precedent that lane set the same day for its own date and that challenger-job-cuts-2026-09-03 set before it: a private publisher's own release schedule is a primary source, not an aggregator reporting one. Corroborated two ways this session: the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet (82 dated rows 2025-12-23 -> 2026-12-23) schedules NO vintage on 2026-11-12 at all, so nothing contradicts NAR's own row; and the seven 2026 EHS dates the GDPNow ContribArchives free text names (01-14, 02-12, 03-10, 04-13, 05-11, 06-09, 07-09) match NAR's published 2026 schedule 7 for 7, which is the same validation the sibling lane ran. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The CONTROL edition for the confound that makes existing-home-sales-2026-12-09 unreadable: that print shares its session with the December SEP decision, whose 14:00 statement takes 85.8% of SPY's session range. This one does not. Verified three ways on 2026-09-06, each an independent axis of confounding, and all three clear: (1) the Federal Reserve's own 2026 panel lists eight meetings — Jan 27-28, Mar 17-18, Apr 28-29, Jun 16-17, Jul 28-29, Sep 15-16, Oct 27-28, Dec 8-9 — and NONE in November, so 11-12 sits 15 days after one decision and 27 before the next; (2) sessions two trading days after a CPI print (11-12 is CPI+2 behind cpi-2026-11-10) are NOT elevated — ITB median session range 1.703% against a 1.847% baseline across 111 instances, permutation p=0.12, if anything quieter; (3) the session after a bond-market-only holiday (11-12 follows sifma-bond-market-closure-2026-11-11) is at baseline for homebuilders — ITB 1.820% vs 1.840% across 17 instances, p=0.92, while the holiday session itself is measurably QUIETER (1.281%, p=0.033). What it is NOT is a bare session: Census releases Business Formation Statistics at the same 10:00 slot (A202611121000, October data) and the Monthly Treasury Statement (mts-october-2026-11-12) lands 14:00. Neither is a homebuilder channel. `symbols: []` and impact `low` are carried on this session's own re-derivation of the sibling's measurement, not on its authority: across 123 EHS release days since 2016 (the 140 GDPNow-archive dates plus 2026-08-11 from NAR's calendar) ITB reads a median session range of 1.927% against a 1.840% baseline (p=0.32), XHB 1.677% vs 1.632% (p=0.60) and SPY 0.893% vs 0.876% (p=0.79) — inert on all three, reproducing the sibling's 1.911/1.839/0.894/0.874 to within a few thousandths on independently pulled bars. The one thing this edition can do that 12-09 cannot is carry the sibling's own inertness kill switch (ITB session range >3.0% on a clean EHS day), and this session measured that switch's power rather than inheriting it: 3.0% is cleared by 16.5% of ordinary sessions unconditionally but only 4.3% at VIX<=16, so the trigger is a p95-class test in today's VIX-14.5 regime and close to a coin flip in a stressed one. Date is `confirmed` on the publisher's own calendar; that licenses nothing, and the ledger's call is stand aside on every horizon. Discovered in the existing-home-sales-2026-12-09 sweep 2026-09-06; canonical file written by this event's own initial research the same day, which shadows that proposal.
